newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Foreign loans boost SAfrica govt financing for Oct.
newsitem.headline: Foreign loans boost SAfrica govt financing for Oct.

text.p: Total Foreign loans of 2.85 billion rand boosted the South African government's financing for October, bringing to 5.76 billion rand the total financing for the month, the Finance Department said on Monday.

Financing of 3.6 billion rand was obtained in government bonds, while net short-term loans decreased by 715.8 million rand, it said in a statement releasing its provisional financing figures for October.
The finance department added government bonds and debentures of 8.712 million rand and foreign loans of 748 million rand were redeemed in the first seven months (April-October 1996).

NOTE - (1) Short-term debt of the former black homelands and self-governing territories, which is refinanced by an increase in Tender Bills. (2) Amounts invested by the CPD usually fluctuate during the course of the financial year.
